chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a man who made a false accusation against a group all together, so he lashed him with one hadd punishment.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The proper way to understand this report is that if he accused them with a single expression, then one hadd punishment became obligatory upon him. But if he falsely accused them with different expressions, he would administer a hadd punishment for each man among them. Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام has detailed that in the narration of al-Ḥasan al-‘Aṭṭār, and what he narrated further clarifies that:

key_terms.بِكَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: with a single expression or statement
key_terms.قَذَفَهُمْ: he accused them of illicit sexual wrongdoing
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: he would enforce or carry out
key_terms.ٱفْتَرَى: made a false accusation or fabricated a slanderous claim

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd ruling if someone falsely accuses a group of people together?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the legal ruling for false accusation against multiple people. It indicates that when the accusation is made in one single expression, one hadd punishment applies, while the accompanying explanation clarifies that separate expressions may entail separate hadd punishments for each person.
